key_insight: An independent certificate checker provides guaranteed error bounds for PDE solver outputs, including finite-element solutions and neural predictions, without trusting the solver.
engineering_relevance: Certificate-based verification can help engineers detect misleadingly converged simulations and assess surrogate predictions against a specified physics model.
method: Return an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current with each prediction.
Use a small independent checker to compute guaranteed error bounds.
Apply the same checker to conventional, LLM-written, and neural solvers.
evidence_signal: The checker rejected or refuted five bugs that passed grid-convergence studies; reduced-basis neural predictions received bounds at most 0.0021% wide in-range and 0.3–25% wide out-of-range.
watch_item: Guarantees apply only to the stated model; informative bounds require energy-accurate outputs on a sufficiently resolving grid.
paper_title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
